annotation.title_clean: 49 U.S. Code § 44809 - Exception for limited recreational operations of unmanned aircraft
annotation.title_en: 49 U.S. Code § 44809 - Exception for limited recreational operations of unmanned aircraft
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States Congress (Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. Code)
annotation.venue: Cornell Legal Information Institute / U.S. Code
annotation.summary_en: US statute creating an exception allowing recreational drone flights without FAA certification if conditions are met: visual line of sight, 400 ft ceiling, community-based organization safety guidelines, registration, and a knowledge test. It also covers fixed sites and educational use, as amended in 2024.
key_provisions_or_claims: Recreational drones exempt from certification if flown within visual line of sight, below 400 ft in Class G airspace, and giving way to manned aircraft
Operators must pass an aeronautical knowledge and safety test and register and mark the aircraft
Controlled airspace flights require prior FAA authorization
Fixed-site operations are approved by the FAA, and aircraft of 55 lb or more must meet community-based organization standards
2024 amendments extend recreational status to educational and research use and preserve FAA enforcement authority
